items.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I mean the song “Cloudburst” was that based on a Wardell Gray solo?

ctx.x: If I can jump back for one minute — I have to ask you about “Cloudburst.” I mean the song “Cloudburst” was that based on a Wardell Gray solo?

No, no. That’s a tragic story. Because you know, all of the guys that came out of the band when the big bands began to break up, you know Chic Webb’s band, all of them went into some aspect of the music business to try to continue to make a living with music. And Chic Webb’s guitarist, his name was Leroy Kirkland. And he was one of Chic Webb’s main arrangers you know, a fine musician. And he was around Broadway trying to make a living selling songs, writing songs, conducting rhythm & blues recording dates you…

items.title: Jon Hendricks — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: There were some wonderful musicians in Detroit. Wardell Gray, Billy Mitchell.

ctx.x: Yeah. There were some wonderful musicians in Detroit. Wardell Gray, Billy Mitchell. Some wonderful horn players too.
